Appearance:
Smt. Meena Singhal- learned Counsel for appellants/ claimants.
Shri Bal Krishna Agrawal- learned Counsel for respondent No.3/ Insurance
Company.

This miscellaneous appeal under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been filed by claimants (father and mother of deceased) against the Award dated 01-02-2021 passed by Sixth Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Gwalior in Claims Case No.716 of 2019, for enhancement of compensation amount.
(2) Facts of case, in short, are that on the alleged date of accident i.e. on 05.05.2019, Shahil (since deceased) aged around 08 years and 04 months, was going to Banmore Village on bicycle.
His father- Ahsan (appellant No.2 herein) and Shadil were following him on their bicycles.
Deceased Shahil was riding his bicycle slowly on road.

As soon as his bicycle reached AB Road in front of Banmore Village at about 3:30 pm, at the same time, a truck bearing registration no. RJ 11-GB-4836 dashed bicycle of Shahil from his back, driven by respondent No.1 very rashly and negligently as a result of which Shahil sustained serious injuries in the accident.

Thereafter,
information of incident was given to Banmore Police by passersby.

Then Shahil was brought to J.A.
Hospital Gwalior where he was being treated for his serious injuries but he died during treatment.
His dead body was sent for postmortem.
All liabilities are on Insurance Company of owner of offending vehicle/ truck (respondent No.2).
On the above grounds, appellants/ claimants filed a claim petition before the Claims Tribunal for compensation along with interest.
After hearing the pleadings of the parties and documents available therein, the Claims Tribunal awarded compensation to the tune of Rs.3,91,000/- in favour of claimants/ appellants.
(3) Being dissatisfied with the impugned Award, the present miscellaneous appeal is filed at the instance of appellants/ claimants for awarding just and proper amount of compensation.

(4) Heard learned Counsel for the parties and perused the impugned award as well as documents available on record.
(5) The date of accident, negligence and issue of liability are not in dispute and the findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal in this regard are clear.

(6) In the case of Kusmi Devi vs. Md. Kasim and Another reported in 2023 ACJ 1658, the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that so far as the question of quantum of compensation in fatal accident is concerned, the regular parameters of assessing compensation cannot be considered in such cases due to uncertainties in life of a child (who was aged 3 years) and enhanced compensation by Rs.1 lac.

sentences.text: (7) Admittedly, in the present matter, where the regular parameters of determining the compensation cannot be considered due to the uncertainties of a child, therefore, in the light of judgment passed by Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Kusmi Devi (supra) and without prejudice to the contentions of both the parties, in the interest of justice, this Court deems it appropriate to grant a further sum of Rs.1, 00,000/- (Rupees one lac) as global enhancement, which shall be deposited by the respondent No.3/Insurance Company before the Claims Tribunal concerned within a period of three weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order whereupon the enhanced amount shall be disbursed to the claimants/appellants.
The enhanced amount shall bear interest at the same rate, as awarded by the Claims Tribunal.
The other findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal shall remain intact.
(8) In view of aforesaid, this misc. appeal stands disposed of.
